items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: Wellman Braud was the first bass player I became conscious of.

ctx.x: Well, there may not be anything in Atlantic City, because Atlantic City was a small place. But I was thinking to some of the things that inspired, when I was in school some of the things I used to listen to. Naturally, Duke Ellington was first. But there was Claude Hopkins and Don Redman, and there was another band around New York called the Santo Domingans, and that was made up mostly of Cubans and guys from Barbados and Latin Americans, but you know, they played good swing music.

But Claude Hopkins... Wellman Braud was the first bass player I became conscious of. And Claude Hopkins had a bass player, I don't know his name to this day, but I'm sure I borrowed something from him. He used to play high on the neck of the bass, you know, and during this time very few guys could do that -- because they were stuck in the first two or three positions.
